pa_revolutionary_ridge_boulders.blurb: A small bouldering zone inside Philadelphia's Wissahickon Valley Park, on the far bank of the creek from the Forbidden Drive lot. Around two dozen problems sit on a wooded ridge of local schist, which makes for a quiet, green setting despite being in the city. Grades run from V0 up to a V7, with the bulk of problems between V0 and V4, so there is something for newer boulderers and a handful of harder tests for strong ones. The park gets busy with hikers and cyclists in good weather, so expect company on the trail even if the boulders are empty.
pa_revolutionary_ridge_boulders.approach: From the Forbidden Drive lot, cross the creek: either double back after the first bridge along the drive, or follow the trail that runs beneath the Henry Avenue bridge.

pa_main_area_the.blurb: The busiest cluster of problems at Hunter's Rocks, a boulder-only ridge in central Pennsylvania's Rocky Ridge Natural Area, west of Frew Road. Roughly two dozen problems are tallied here, spread over several named boulders, and the difficulty range is wide: plenty of V0 to V3 lines for warming up, a middle group around V4 to V6, and a few much harder problems at the top end. It is a good place for a mixed group, since easy and hard problems share the same hillside.

pa_main_wall_4.blurb: The principal cliff at the downriver end of Chickies Rock, above the Susquehanna near Marietta and Columbia. About twenty traditional lines share this quartzite face, along with one top-rope problem, and the cliff stands around 150 feet. Most routes are moderate, clustering at 5.4 and from 5.7 to 5.8, with a few 5.9s and one 5.11 for stronger leaders. A broad ledge partway up is a favourite for rigging top ropes, which also makes it crowded when several parties turn up. The face is open and sunny, and the river views are a bonus.
pa_main_wall_4.parking_note: Leave the car in the Furnace Road lot for the river trail; signs from Route 441 in Marietta lead to it.
pa_main_wall_4.approach: Walk the river trail downstream, heading east and then south, and cross the Chiques Creek bridge. The paved path continues to the cliff; the Main Wall is at its south end.

pa_f_big_wall.blurb: The tallest and steepest section of Birdsboro Quarry, an old diabase quarry in southeastern Pennsylvania. This is a hard-sport wall: about two dozen bolted lines, mostly from 5.11 through 5.13, with only a few easier options in the 5.9 to 5.10 range. Because the rock was cut by machine, expect some loose material and look closely at holds. A few lines use two sets of anchors, and a 60 metre rope handles most of them. You reach it by walking past a string of smaller walls, then looking up at the big overhanging rock above.

pa_2_5_alpine_wall_aka_tall_wall.blurb: A tall buttress, about 180 feet, on the Safe Harbor North stretch of cliffs above the Susquehanna River, reached along the rail trail. Around twenty routes here are mostly bolted, plus a few traditional and top-rope lines. Difficulty runs from about 5.6 to 5.12, with the greatest concentration at 5.10, so it suits intermediate climbers best. A popular outing links a longer first pitch to a shorter second pitch. The lines are longer than at many neighbouring walls, and the setting along the river is quiet compared with the trailhead area.
